correctness.rationale: Nifa's peripheral map sends the natural tangent generators to \(\lambda\) and \(\lambda^{-N}\), so \(a[\lambda_r]+b[s_r]\) represents \(\lambda^{a-Nb}\). Nifa proves that \(\lambda\) is a commutator and that \(\operatorname{scl}(\lambda^N)=(N-1)/2\). Homogeneity gives \(\operatorname{scl}(\lambda)=(N-1)/(2N)\), hence the stated absolute-value formula. Liu--Ni--Sun--Wang identify their induced slope seminorm with stable commutator length and uniquely extend it to real homology. For a primitive integral slope with \(a-Nb=Nq\ne0\), Nifa's exact commutator-length formula plus his singular-genus lemma gives the stated ceiling formula.

value.rationale: This computes a natural invariant on the entire two-dimensional slope space of a newly constructed same-exterior family, rather than only on the single direction treated in the source. The rational-strip formula exposes the exact kernel and shows that the complete stable slope invariant is identical across \(N\) pairwise ambient-homeomorphism-inequivalent tori. That gives a precise limitation of slope-seminorm detection in an important new complement problem, while the index-\(N\) sublattice retains exact singular-genus values.
